name: 2566-longprefill-mistral7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1). The quantization path's minimum compute capability at this commit is 75, which this card clears.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One in-process engine. 4.15 GB of packed weights against 0.9 * 80 GB leaves roughly 66 GiB of KV cache, about 540k tokens at 128 KiB/token.
architecture: Dense decoder (MistralForCausalLM), 32 layers, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads (GQA 4:1), head_dim 128, hidden 4096, intermediate 14336, vocab 32000, rope_theta 1e6, `sliding_window: null`, native context 32768, fp16 activations over 4-bit packed weights. KV per token = 2 * 32 * 8 * 128 * 2 B = 128 KiB. Packed weights are 4.15 GB on disk. Read off the published config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=100, bounded at 600 requests / 1200 s safety, warmup the first 20% by completion. 100 sits below `max-num-seqs: 256`, so the scheduler admits every in-flight stream and the operating point is set by the load profile rather than by an engine ceiling. Residency is ~1088 tokens per stream, so 100 streams hold ~109k tokens against a ~540k-token pool: this run cannot preempt or swap. CONCURRENCY IS PART OF THE SETUP. This engine has no chunked prefill, so a prompt is always processed whole, and `max-num-batched-tokens` derives to 2048, which is exactly two 1024-token prompts -- the size of a prompt-processing step is therefore fixed by the prompt length and not by the depth of the loop, and the depth's job is only to keep the queue non-empty.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, prompt EXACTLY 1024 tokens (min = max = 1024) and output EXACTLY 64 tokens (min = max = 64), 600 requests, static seed 2551. Raw prompts (`request_format: plain`), no chat template, so the engine sees exactly 1024 prompt tokens. Fixed-length synthetic prompts rather than a scraped dataset; both lengths are pinned to a single value rather than a distribution. The backend turns the declared output length into `max_tokens=64` with `ignore_eos=True`, so every request generates exactly 64 tokens and the number of decode steps is fixed by the declaration. THE MIX IS 94% PROMPT TOKENS: 1024 in, 64 out, so of the 1088 tokens a request touches, 1024 are processed in one prompt step and 64 one at a time. That ratio is the workload's defining property.
purpose: A document-analysis assistant on one GPU summarizing 1000-word briefs into short answers for 100 concurrent users.
launch:
# ENGINE: 390b495ff327e8548c3f7cd701afce87870d9102 -- `git describe --tags` says
#   v0.2.7-61-g390b495ff3 (2024-01-26). A commit, not a release, so the engine is a source
#   checkout named by configs/env.yaml `venv:`.
#
# SEMANTICS: a prefill-heavy serving point on one card against a 4-bit AWQ (W4A16) checkpoint.
# Long prompt, short reply, a deep closed loop: the engine spends most of its wall clock in
# prompt processing rather than in generation. Nothing here is tuned, there is no tuned.yaml,
# and no vLLM knob is declared tunable.
#
# ERA HAZARD: every key here becomes an `AsyncEngineArgs(**kwargs)` keyword and this engine's
# EngineArgs has 30 fields -- there is NO enable_prefix_caching, NO enable_chunked_prefill, NO
# kv_cache_dtype and NO max_logprobs, so writing any of them out, even as its later default,
# is a TypeError on this engine.

# --- The setup's model, ungated and public (`gated=False`, `private=False` on the HF API).
# MistralForCausalLM, 32 layers, 32 query heads, 8 KV heads (GQA 4:1), head_dim 128, hidden
# 4096, intermediate 14336, vocab 32000, rope_theta 1e6, sliding_window null, native context
# 32768, fp16. 4-bit AWQ, group_size 128, zero_point true, GEMM packing; one 4.15 GB
# safetensors shard. KV per token = 2 * 32 * 8 * 128 * 2 B = 128 KiB.
model: TheBloke/Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2-AWQ

# --- W4A16. The checkpoint IS quantized and the engine has to be told so; this is the setup,
# not a knob. At this commit the AWQ config is read from the repo's `quant_config.json`
# (w_bit 4, q_group_size 128, zero_point true) rather than from config.json's
# `quantization_config` block. Minimum compute capability 75; H100 is 90.
quantization: awq

# --- One card, one in-process engine. 4.15 GB of packed weights against an 80 GB board leaves
# essentially the whole board for KV.
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# --- The only activation dtype this quantization path accepts at this commit
# (`get_supported_act_dtypes() -> [torch.half]`), and the checkpoint's own
# `torch_dtype: float16`. Pinned so `auto` cannot drift it.
dtype: float16

# --- 1024 prompt + 64 output. 1088 is the smallest window that lets the declared output
# actually be produced, which is what guidellm needs in order for a request to complete
# normally rather than be truncated.
max-model-len: 1088

# --- This engine's own default (256), written out because it is the ceiling on the closed
# loop: it sits well above the 100 declared streams, so the scheduler is never the thing
# limiting residency and the operating point is set by the load profile alone.
max-num-seqs: 256

# --- This engine's own default (0.90) written out. It decides the KV pool and therefore how
# much of the declared concurrency stays resident. At 0.9 of an 80 GB board minus 4.15 GB of
# packed weights the pool is roughly 66 GiB, about 540k tokens at 128 KiB/token -- about five
# times the ~109k tokens 100 resident streams of 1088 need, so this run cannot preempt or swap.
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.9

# --- This engine's own default (16), written out so the block-table shape is fixed.
block-size: 16

# --- This engine's own default (4 GiB), written out for the same reason. The operating point
# is sized not to swap; this only pins the pool.
swap-space: 4

# --- This engine's own default (0), written out. It seeds vLLM's sampler; guidellm's synthetic
# workload does not pin a temperature, so leaving this implicit would make the token stream
# depend on an unstated default.
seed: 0

# --- DELIBERATELY ABSENT:
#   max-num-batched-tokens -- left at the engine's derived default, max(max_model_len, 2048)
#                             = 2048. It is what sizes a prompt-processing step here: two
#                             1024-token prompts fill it exactly, and this engine has no
#                             chunked prefill, so a prompt is always processed whole.
#   max-paddings           -- this engine's default (256); nothing here depends on it.
#   enforce-eager          -- left False, the default, so decode is CUDA-graph captured.
#   tokenizer              -- defaults to `model`, which is the checkpoint's own tokenizer.
#   trust-remote-code      -- MistralForCausalLM is in this engine's registry.
#   pipeline-parallel-size / worker-use-ray -- 1 GPU, one process, no Ray.
#   more GPUs              -- 1 GPU is the topology, not a scaling-down.
